formula_extraction.method: The workbook is a legacy .xls (BIFF8 / OLE Compound File). xlrd's public API (open_workbook / Sheet.cell) only exposes each formula cell's last-cached VALUE, not its formula text. This script (1) uses olefile to read the raw 'Workbook' BIFF stream, (2) walks it to find the FORMULA record (type 0x0006) for each pollutant's Sub-Index cell and extracts its raw rgce token bytes, then (3) calls xlrd.formula.decompile_formula — xlrd's own internal (undocumented but public-importable) RPN-token decompiler — to render the token stream as a readable formula string. This is xlrd's real formula engine, not a hand-rolled parser.
formula_extraction.verification_of_raw_bytes: Beyond decompile_formula's output, the O3 formula's two occurrences of the constant 539 were independently re-verified by scanning the raw rgce bytes for PtgInt (0x1e) tokens directly and unpacking them as little-endian u16 — both are genuine 2-byte integer literals in the byte stream (at offsets 248 and 288 within that formula's token stream), not a decompiler rendering artifact.

structural_finding.summary: Every pollutant except O3 decodes to the SAME shape: five finite tiers (identical numbers to the CPCB 2014 Good..Very-Poor bands, and identical to ingest/app/aqi.py's tiers 1-5), followed by an UNCONDITIONAL final IF(C > tier5_ceiling, ...) branch that extends TIER 5's OWN slope indefinitely. There is no sixth, distinct 'Severe' tier with its own ceiling and slope anywhere in the workbook — repo_current's breakpoint tables all have an extra (tier5_ceiling, X, 400, 500) tuple that the real formula does not contain. Whether that extra tuple's SLOPE happens to match tier 5's real slope (by the tier ceiling X being chosen consistently) determines whether repo_current's severe-band OUTPUT happens to be right or wrong even though its TABLE SHAPE is wrong either way.

o3_discontinuity.status: workbook formula artifact under investigation — NOT confirmed CPCB policy or intentional design
o3_discontinuity.summary: O3's real tier 5 is (208,748,300,400) — same numbers ingest/app/aqi.py uses — but its own divisor is the literal integer 539, not 748-208=540 (a 1-unit-short off-by-one, confirmed as a genuine byte-level constant, not a decoding artifact). Its tail term for C>748 is 400.0+(C-400.0)*100.0/539.0 — note the anchor is 400, NOT 748 (the tier boundary) and NOT 208. A correctly-continuous formula would anchor on 748 (i.e. 400+(C-748)*100/539). Because it anchors on 400 instead, the formula JUMPS upward by roughly 64 AQI points at C=748: the tier-5 branch gives ~400.19 at C=748 itself, and the very next value above 748 evaluates to ~464.56.
o3_discontinuity.interpretation: A plausible hypothesis is an authoring typo in the original 2014/2015 spreadsheet (748 mistyped as 400, and/or 540 mistyped as 539), but this is unconfirmed and this manifest does not assert it as fact. This harness's job is to transcribe the workbook faithfully, not silently fix or explain away what it decoded.
o3_discontinuity.how_this_harness_handles_it: profiles/cpcb_workbook_formula_exact.py's _o3_sub_index_uncapped implements the decoded formula EXACTLY, divisor and anchor included, with no correction applied. Every O3 evaluation above 748 carries an unconditional 'unresolved: workbook formula artifact under investigation...' warning (see tests/test_o3_discontinuity.py), on top of the pre-existing 'O3 averaging behaviour above 208' warning the harness brief specifically asked to keep unresolved.

rounding.method: round-half-up (math.floor(raw + 0.5)), applied once per pollutant to the raw sub-index
rounding.confidence: Corroborated by both the worked example (NH3=34 -> raw 8.5 -> rounds to 9, not Python's banker's-rounding 8) and, now, by the decoded formula text itself not specifying any rounding at all inside the sub-index cell formula — the workbook's Sub-Index column (D) is unrounded (matches the raw 56.666... and 8.5 values extracted in v1's worked-example check); rounding is presumably applied at cell-display-format level (a formatting concern, not a formula concern) or by whatever consumes the sheet's output. This harness applies round-half-up explicitly since that is what ingest/app/aqi.py's own prior verification against this same file established and what the raw half-integer example confirms.

cap_policy.repo_current: Hard clamp to 500 for any concentration above the top breakpoint tier (ingest/app/aqi.py:102, `return 500`) — confirmed by direct code read.
cap_policy.cpcb_workbook_formula_exact: CONFIRMED uncapped — directly from the decoded formula text. Every pollutant's IF-chain ends in an unconditional `IF(C > tier5_ceiling, formula)` with no further condition and no reference to 500 anywhere in any of the 7 formulas. There is no cap logic in this workbook to have missed.

display_policy_above_500.position: Still deliberately unresolved. This harness does not assume what CPCB's public dashboards (e.g. airquality.cpcb.gov.in, app.cpcbccr.com) would actually show for a reading whose mathematical sub-index exceeds 500 — this workbook is a calculator, not those dashboards, and nothing here speaks to their display behaviour. See models.ProfileResult.display_value / category_label, both None whenever rounded_sub_index > 500.
